principles: Scope contract is gate input and current-state policy, not a replacement for process-events or evidence history.
Default compatibility: no contract should not break existing stories unless strict policy explicitly opts in.
All human/agent paths use CLI schemas and handlers so runner-specific tooling reuses the same checks.
Out-of-scope changes must be visible to reviewers and tests; no silent expansion.
drivers: Prevent AI agents from modifying existing functionality outside agreed scope.
Avoid false blocks for old stories and small local/shadow workflows.
Provide focused smoke tests that future milestones can reuse as protected regression fixtures.

options.name: contract-plus-post-diff-gate
pros: Creates a reusable mechanical policy source for Claude/Codex/Gemini runners.
Works with existing lifecycle gates and can start in compatibility mode.
Produces concrete terminal output for reviewers and users.
cons: Requires new persistence, CLI commands, and lifecycle integration in one story.
Needs careful tests to avoid blocking old stories incorrectly.

options.name: claude-hook-first
pros: Can block Claude Code edits earlier before files change.
Directly targets the tool the user asked about.
cons: Would create a Claude-specific policy before Koala has a provider-neutral source of truth.
Codex/Gemini and server-side gates would still need separate implementations.

options.name: reviewer-only-diff-check
pros: Lower implementation cost and minimal lifecycle changes.
cons: Still relies on reviewer discipline and can miss automated TEST/DONE bypasses.
Does not provide a hard pre-merge gate.

rationale: Choose the provider-neutral contract first because every later pre-tool or regression policy needs the same canonical scope decision and terminal output.

preMortem.scenario: Old stories without scope contracts start failing REVIEW or DONE unexpectedly.
preMortem.trigger: Lifecycle gate treats missing contract as enforce by default.
preMortem.consequence: Existing active or repair stories get blocked for unrelated reasons.
preMortem.mitigation: Use compatibility default: missing contract is pass/warn unless strict policy explicitly requires one; add smoke coverage.

preMortem.scenario: Agent bypasses scope by expanding the allowed paths after making changes.
preMortem.trigger: scope change command mutates contract without reason or reviewer-visible record.
preMortem.consequence: Out-of-scope edits become invisible to reviewers and defeat the purpose of the gate.
preMortem.mitigation: Require acknowledgement reason, actor, timestamp, and added paths; render acknowledgement in check/review output and test it.

preMortem.scenario: Scope gate checks the wrong diff base or ignores untracked files.
preMortem.trigger: Implementation only inspects committed diff or assumes main...HEAD is enough in all phases.
preMortem.consequence: Uncommitted or newly created out-of-scope files can pass local checks.
preMortem.mitigation: Scope check must inspect committed and worktree changes where appropriate; smoke tests include create/modify paths.

preMortem.scenario: The new gate duplicates story history and becomes another stale truth source.
preMortem.trigger: Contract stores full lifecycle logs instead of current scope policy and references.
preMortem.consequence: Agents disagree about whether story/process-events/evidence or scope contract is authoritative.
preMortem.mitigation: Limit scope contract to current policy plus acknowledgement refs; leave lifecycle history in process-events/evidence.
